newsitem.title: UK: British Millennium celebrations on track.
newsitem.headline: British Millennium celebrations on track.

text.p: The British government said on Friday it had reached agreement with the opposition Labour Party to ensure that ambitious plans to celebrate the Millennium go ahead, whichever party is in power.
The Department of National Heritage, in charge of the project, said it had struck a deal with Labour, hot favourites to win Britain's election which must be held by May 22.
The two sides held talks this week in an effort to ensure that plans for a 750 million pound ($1.26 billion) exhibition at Greenwich, London, stayed on track, politics aside.
Backers of the project, at the heart of which is a huge dome to be built on reclaimed land, had said that business sponsors might pull out if Labour did not endorse the scheme soon.
Labour, however, was wary of being landed with a huge bill and wanted a guarantee it could review the plans once in power.

After repeated wrangling, the Times newspaper said in its Saturday editions that Deputy Prime Minister Michael Heseltine and Labour leader Tony Blair had finally agreed on a formula that was expected to win approval from the Millennium Commission on Saturday.
"We are delighted that the exhibition is going ahead," it quoted a Heseltine spokesman as saying.
A Labour spokesman said discussions were continuing but that he was confident of an announcement on Saturday.
